content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to [product_name]. I attempted to set up a master-slave communication in the Network Project section of [product_name] [product_name], but couldn't find an option to write programs in Ladder Logic. Could someone advise me on this? Thanks in advance.
Within a network project, only FBD programming is available.
Check the attached file—it's a page from the manual.
If you want to create ladder programs, you'll need to manually configure network settings so each [product_name] receives its own program file. You can refer to a thread like this for an example.

Hi [user_name], I've tried your explanation regarding ladder diagrams in [product_name] [version_no], but I haven't managed to make it work. I made the same mistake, already programmed quite a lot in ladder, and now switching to FBD is getting complicated. You mentioned changing hardware settings to enable ladder programming in networks, but I'm not sure how to do this. Is there a way? If so, could you guide me?

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. Attached are a video and two ladder diagrams. These show how to set up a master/master communication between two [product_name] units. One acts as the client (active) and the other as the server (passive).

Thank you for your response. I now see how to configure for simulation in the network, but please review the screenshot—I'm unable to import my ladder diagram into the logic module. Second question: with FBD, there is access to 400 memory blocks internally. Does this block limit also apply to ladder diagrams?

If you've read the topic from the start, you probably saw my earlier reply explaining this—importing LAD programs into a network project isn't possible. Regarding your other question: If you're asking about the number of available blocks, with a [product_name] [article_no], there are always 400 blocks available, whether using LAD or FBD.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced restrictions when attempting to use Ladder Logic (LAD) within the Network Project feature of [product_name] [product_name], as only Function Block Diagram (FBD) is supported in that context. This limitation surprised many, especially those hoping to import existing LAD programs, which led to confusion and complications in their workflow. Attempts to adjust hardware settings or integrate LAD diagrams into network projects were unsuccessful.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate being able to program in Ladder Logic within the Network Project feature and wish to import existing LAD diagrams into network projects. They also seek clarification regarding the capabilities and block limits when using LAD versus FBD programming modes.
